review_notes: Principal family selected from the abstract/introduction and primary design: Equation (6), Table 6 future-performance regressions. The introduction frames the central contribution as the association of real activities manipulation with firms just meeting earnings benchmarks and the subsequent performance of those firms; Equation (6) directly tests that question. The eight t+1 columns are retained as parallel outcomes (AdjROA, AdjCFO) and RM measures (R&D, SG&A, production, aggregate). Earlier benchmark-incidence tests, descriptive analyses, and the asset-RM column in the separate hypothesis-1 analysis are outside this principal family. Equation (6) states i=1,2,3, but the paper calls t+2/t+3 results robustness and Table 6 reports t+1, so later horizons are not separate baseline entries.

Source conflict: Equation (6) and the Table 6 coefficient row identify the current performance control as AdjROA_t, while the equation printed in the Table 6 header labels it ROA_t. The extraction uses AdjROA_t, supported by Equation (6) and the row label, and preserves the header conflict in model review notes.

Source numbering conflict: the Aggregate RM definition calls its production component “production model 3” multiplied by −1, while the displayed production-cost regression is Equation (4), and individual Production RM definitions identify model 4. The aggregate construction therefore preserves the paper’s wording and flags the inconsistent model number; the production-cost fit is retained as the required construction dependency.

Equation (1) timing conflict: its paragraph says estimates cover 1988–2000, while the general Table 1 estimation description states 1988–2002 for equations 1–4. Both statements are preserved for the R&D construction fit.
results_review_notes: Retained family is the eight Table 6 t+1 fits only: four RM samples in Panel A and the same four in Panel B. Untabulated t+2 and t+3 results and Table 5 correlations are excluded.
Table 6 p.27 equation prints ROA_t for the performance control, while Eq. (6) p.22 and the table coefficient row identify AdjROA_t; the retained row is linked to local iv_006 AdjROA_t.
Table 6 equation and the base specification use ZSCORE_{t−1}, while the Table 6 coefficient row prints ZSCORE_t. Preserve the printed row label and link it to local iv_010 ZSCORE_{t−1}.

The aggregate RM definition labels the production residual model 3 multiplied by −1, whereas the production-cost equation and Production RM definition identify model 4. Preserve this source numbering inconsistency.

Page 26 explicitly reports p<0.001 for the Panel A R&D-sample BENCH_t coefficient and a γ0+γ1 fitted AdjROA_{t+1} point estimate of −0.050. The latter has no reported inference and is stored as an auxiliary row in the existing fit.
Page 26 describes the Table 4 benchmark average as 0.055; the R&D sample BEAT row in Table 4 displays 5.2 for AdjROA_{t+1}. Both are preserved as printed without reconciliation.

Table 2 Panel A residual summaries are retained for the R&D, SG&A, and production residual inputs used to construct the selected RM flags; Gain Asset residuals do not feed a retained baseline variable and are excluded. Their residual units are not the binary RM scale.

Table 4 Assets (millions) summaries are retained as raw-version descriptives for SIZE_t. Its category sample counts exceed the Table 6 fit Ns; sample overlap with the complete-case fits is therefore left unclear.
No direct descriptive table or prose summary of AdjCFO_{t+1} was located. Table 2 Panel B and Table 5 correlations are not variable-descriptive statistics.
